documents.title: Generative AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page offers three template statements (open, moderate, closed) and says 'faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI', leaving the choice to instructors. A document offering tiers or templates is coded delegates.
tiers: Open Use: Permitted in this Course with Attribution
Moderate Use: Permitted when Assigned in this Course with Attribution
Closed: Not Permitted in this Course
documents.summary: Teaching-center page giving faculty three ready-to-paste syllabus statements, from open use with attribution to a closed ban treated as misconduct. It also warns users not to share sensitive data with AI tools.

units.why: The page recommends that faculty state AI expectations in their syllabi: "We recommend clearly outlining when and how students should use these tools". It is a recommendation to instructors about communicating rules, so P09 with modality should.
units.anchor: We recommend clearly outlining when and how students should use these tools within your courses.
units.frag_start: We recommend clearly outlining when
units.fit_note: A recommendation, not a requirement, to state AI expectations.

units.why: "Depending on the course, faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI" says the rule varies by instructor and course, so P04, an informing statement.
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all/phase general; B coded actor instructor/phase before-course. The sentence ('Depending on the course, faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI') is a general statement about variation across courses, not addressed to one actor at one point, so all/general.

documents.title: Faculty Handbook - AI in Higher Education (introduces Policy 220)
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI-use stance itself: it introduces Policy 220 as 'authoritative' and points to syllabus statements and resources. The rule text is elsewhere, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Handbook page introducing Policy 220, the state-mandated AI policy for instruction and assignments, without reproducing its rules. It lists the AI Task Force outcomes, AI Academy, MInDS Center and syllabus statements.

units.why: "Tennessee Tech is committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date and are equipped with the knowledge and resources" states an institution-level commitment and purpose, so P56 (framework/preamble).
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral, B encourage. The sentence commits the university to keeping people 'up-to-date and equipped with the knowledge and resources'; it does not itself welcome or recommend AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: Tennessee Tech is committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date
units.frag_start: As generative AI continues to evolve
units.fit_note: Also commits to equipping the community with knowledge and resources to use generative AI.

units.why: The page cites state law: institutions "must adopt a policy" on AI use by students, faculty and staff by July 1, 2025. This is a legal mandate behind Policy 220, so P77 (comply with existing law).
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded must (with a normalized policy). The page reports what state law requires ('institutions must adopt a policy ... by July 1, 2025') as the reason Policy 220 exists, so it is a fact about the law (informs); P77 in both.
units.anchor: institutions must adopt a policy
units.frag_start: Pursuant to T.C.A. 49-8-203(a); T.C.A.
units.fit_note: A state-law requirement to adopt and post an AI policy, rather than a rule on AI use itself.

units.why: Says Policy 220 'is Tennessee Tech's authoritative resource and takes precedence over any information provided on this website'. It sets the hierarchy among sources; nearest is P80 (who owns the policy), but no type matches exactly.
